images.caption: Front Street in Downtown Traverse City is a charming and vibrant commercial drag that is the symbolic and commercial heart of the Grand Traverse Bay region. Developed initially during the 19th Century

place.source_title: Front Street commercial building with a vertical-fin facade, Traverse City

brief: A two-storey 1960s commercial block with a facade screen of tall vertical cream metal fins, a glazed shopfront and a corner entry, a pickup on the street. One photo. Older than 1970 (c. 1965): the only modernist front on the street. Older than 1970: Petoskey's Gaslight District (the town's model) is a row of 1880-1910 brick commercial blocks; no newer example of this main-street type exists. Foundations taken deeper than needed (spec rule 4).

facade.notes: a Front Street building (Traverse City MI, 1965): a three-storey front refaced in vertical metal fins (a 1960s slipcover) over an older block, with a neighbour's banded front; 'FRONT ROW CENTRE' sign; street trees and outdoor seating

why.note: 1960s fins slipcovered over a Victorian front to look modern
